verdict.rationale: The IRS publishes pieces of a delegation model. The EIN assistant documents a third-party designee role that requires signed authorization from the responsible party (irs-supp-13), and authorized e-file providers are a credentialed intermediary role with a published enrollment path (irs-supp-5, irs-supp-6). Signed mobile-friendly forms such as the 83(b) Form 15620 must be completed through the taxpayer's own ID.me-proofed Online Account, which shows those signatures stay personal (irs-supp-12, irs-supp-9). Missing for 10: named general authorization forms (e.g., power-of-attorney or tax-information authorization documents), a consolidated statement of what representatives may and may not do across services, and an explicit list of which signatures cannot be delegated.
